newsitem.title: USA: New food introductions on the rise.
newsitem.headline: New food introductions on the rise.

text.p: Introductions of new food products in the U.S. retail market, which declined by more than 20 percent in 1996, are on the rise again, the publisher of New Product News magazine said Monday.
Food product introductions thus far in 1997 are close to those logged early in 1995, Lynn Dornblaser told a briefing at the Food Marketing Institute's annual supermarket convention, held in Chicago.
"So far in 1997, new product totals are close to the 1995 level, indicating that companies are re-initiating their new product programmes," Dornblaser said.
At this pace, she added, food product introductions in 1997 will be close to 1995 levels, "but perhaps not that high."
One area that is gaining in popularity is home meal replacement, including fresh, single-serve dishes and meal components.
In 1996, new food product introductions fell to 13,266 from 16,863. That 21 percent decline was the largest drop in 20 years, Dornblaser said.

She attributed the decline, in part, to corporate restructurings and the sale of divisions, both of which tend to reduce new product introductions. In addition, with grocery stores stuffed with products, it remains difficult for mid-sized companies, in particular, to get their new products on the shelves in competition with larger firms.
Smaller food companies tend to launch products through gourmet and speciality stores.

Looking ahead, food companies will continue to launch new products through brand and line extensions, with less emphasis on new brands, according to Carol Elitov, general manager of Information Resources Inc.'s New Product Solution Centre.
She added that food companies also will target products for an ageing population, including more low-fat, high quality foods and dishes that are easily prepared.
